weeks.title: Establish the foundations and the experiment contract
weeks.aim: Understand the robot-learning loop and start the research infrastructure immediately. Diagnose knowledge gaps instead of redoing material already mastered.
days: Diagnose and scope

Spend 90 minutes on the self-assessment. Review MDPs/returns; specify one obstructed manipulation task, its action interface and success rubric. Create the experiment repository and environment manifest.
Bellman and blockage
Implement the blocked-gridworld example. Evaluate a frozen policy before and after a wall change, then replan. Write what changed: environment state, dynamics, policy or action sequence.
Geometry and commands
Implement planar FK/Jacobian checks. Review frame composition and calibration. Inspect the physical arm interface or simulator and record action units, joint limits and control frequency.
Policy gradients
Derive REINFORCE and a baseline. Work through a hand-computed trajectory. Install only the small educational stack in an isolated environment; identify GPU requirements for the research stack.
Task and recorder
Create/reset the simulated scene. Record a scripted policy episode and outcome. Read DayDreamer's problem/method/experiments and sketch how policy learning differs from MPC.
Integrate and explain

Replay an episode, export an initial manifest, and record a five-minute explanation of the full observation→policy→controller loop. Review the week's assumptions and unresolved hardware access issues.
outputs: One-page research question and nominal/blocked task specification.
Working tabular obstruction demo and geometry checks.
One logged simulator episode and a reproducibility manifest.
weeks.gate: A scripted controller can complete one nominal episode and produce replayable data. If hardware is unavailable, continue in simulation while arranging access; do not postpone the model-learning pilot.
weeks.explain: Why does a blockage sometimes require replanning, sometimes a policy update, and sometimes a better world model?

weeks.title: Understand policy optimization; finish the first vertical slice
weeks.aim: Implement enough RL to defend the equations and establish a repeatable task pipeline before increasing model scale.
days: GAE and PPO
Implement returns/GAE and the PPO update. Check terminal versus truncated trajectories manually. Inspect CleanRL's rollout-buffer layout.
A complete RL run
Run a small reference PPO experiment and save all hyperparameters. Inspect losses, entropy, approximate KL and gradient norms. Fix wrapper issues before tuning learning rates.
SAC and replay
Derive the soft Q target and inspect a reference SAC trainer. Run a continuous-control smoke experiment. Explain replay reuse, target networks and tanh action scaling.
Robot data pathway
Finish observation/action logging and the reset procedure. Acquire a few nominal and obstructed diagnostic rollouts. Confirm both success and failure labels are observable.
Read the closest adaptation baseline
Read FOSP's method, real-robot section and limitations. Distinguish learning from real interaction plus imagination from an imagined-only adaptation claim.
Gate 1 review
Demonstrate reset→observe→act→record→replay in the actual task. Present a tensor-level PPO explanation and choose the continuous-control implementation to reuse.
outputs: Original PPO update with numerical checks.
Reference continuous-control run with pinned revision.
End-to-end task recording, including at least one blocked failure.
weeks.gate: The task pipeline and a continuous-action actor execute reliably. Fix integration or simplify the scene now; larger model training does not solve a broken interface.
weeks.explain: How do PPO and SAC differ, and why are imagined transitions not automatically equivalent to real off-policy data?

weeks.title: Build the base policy and the first predictive model
weeks.aim: Get the smallest scientifically useful policy/world-model pair running. Maintain the same task across learning exercises and research.
days: Data and splits

Define training, development/acquisition and held-out test layout IDs before collection. Generate a modest simulation demonstration set. Measure real reset/labeling time before committing to hardware episode counts.
Behavior cloning
Train the nominal BC controller, save normalization statistics, and evaluate closed-loop rollouts. Inspect failure videos rather than choosing checkpoints from training loss alone.
Learn transitions
Fit a small delta-state dynamics ensemble. Keep obstacle pose and relevant contact state observable. Validate one-step transitions on the development split.
Read neural world models
Trace Dreamer posterior/prior and actor training; inspect DINO-WM's action-conditioned feature prediction. Choose one feasible observation/model route using data access and measured runtime.
Paired rollouts
Compare 5/10/20-step model predictions with actual simulator execution from the same start and actions. Read RePLan's obstruction cases as behavior references, not as neural-world-model baselines.
Architecture decision
Freeze the core experiment interface and choose compact actor plus learned dynamics. Document the upgrade path to visual latents or a pretrained world-action model without making it a dependency.
outputs: Nominal BC checkpoint and dataset/split card.
Action-conditioned dynamics ensemble and multi-step error report.
Architecture decision with measured memory/runtime and explicit model-family labels.
weeks.gate: A usable nominal baseline and action-sensitive model predictions exist. If visual modeling is not viable, run the core diagnostic with state observations and label that limitation explicitly.
weeks.explain: What information would a world model need to faithfully simulate your newly introduced blocker?

weeks.title: Make imagination useful; establish the planning baseline
weeks.aim: Verify the model can support decisions and build the strongest simple alternative to policy fine-tuning.
days: Action-conditioned validity
Test zero, permuted and deliberately colliding actions. Check whether prediction errors preserve or erase the obstacle. Add failure data only from training/development scenes.
CEM-MPC
Implement receding-horizon search on the learned model. Log horizon, model calls, elapsed time and the action prefix executed. Keep exact simulator dynamics out of this baseline.
Generative-policy mini-lab
Implement the two-route action denoiser/flow example. Inspect Diffusion Policy and openpi interfaces; separate policy generation from world-model prediction.
Read model failure carefully
Read ReOI's obstacle erasure examples and ten-trial evaluation. Read RISE's policy-improvement loop and compute requirements. Record what these papers do not establish.
Model and planner evaluation
Run nominal and obstructed development trials. Compare frozen policy, random shooting and learned-model MPC. Identify whether failures are model, search or controller failures.
Gate 2 review
Produce a short paired imagination/execution clip and a planner result. Set a small, measured adaptation-time budget and choose a residual actor implementation for Week 5.
outputs: A learned-world-model MPC baseline.
Paired predicted/executed blockage examples.
An explicit decision about whether the model is adequate for an imagined-training pilot.
weeks.gate: The model distinguishes important failed actions from successful ones on development scenes. If it cannot, improve data/representation before optimizing a policy against it.
weeks.explain: Why might a perfect-looking predicted video still be a poor training environment?

weeks.title: Implement the dream→update→execute loop
weeks.aim: Demonstrate genuine policy parameter adaptation from imagined experience, with a fixed model during each adaptation round.
days: Specify the update
Define residual action bounds, replay mixture, rollout horizon, reward/cost terms and actor/critic update counts. Start every condition from the same base actor checkpoint.
Synthetic transitions
Seed short model rollouts from actual development observations. Store predicted transitions in a separate buffer and tag model version, rollout depth and uncertainty.
Fine-tune the actor
Implement the chosen SAC-style update using synthetic transitions and original replay. Check actor weight changes, model freezing and critic targets. Profile a complete update round.
Return to execution
Run the adapted actor in the actual simulator, then hardware if the pipeline is ready. Compare measured success with its imagined estimate and save failure videos.
Retention and limits
Evaluate nominal scenes after adaptation. Test short versus longer imagined horizons. Keep every time limit or rollback in the results, rather than removing unsuccessful runs.
Pilot interpretation

Compare no adaptation, MPC and imagined fine-tuning on a small development suite. Write one page explaining whether the bottleneck is model fidelity, exploration, credit assignment or optimizer stability.
outputs: A reproducible imagination-only actor update.
Measured adaptation latency and real/simulator outcome comparison.
A retention check and one documented failure case.
weeks.gate: At least one complete round executes and yields interpretable measurements. Improvement is a hypothesis, not a gate that justifies changing the test after seeing results.
weeks.explain: Where does the policy gradient or synthetic replay signal come from when the world model is frozen?

weeks.title: Add real verification and freeze the research question
weeks.aim: Finish the six-week preparation period with an honest pilot and a defensible experimental plan. Outreach has not started yet.
days: Detect and represent blockage
Define stagnation/collision/progress checks on development data. Reobserve before adaptation; distinguish current latent-state inference from changing model weights.
Generate candidates
Build a legal correction-trial pool independent of held-out tests. Compare predicted outcomes across ensemble members and compute an initial disagreement score.
Verify physically
Run a small random correction batch, add executed transitions, update the world model between rounds, then repeat imagined actor adaptation. Count reset and human time.
Read related correction work
Read Fail2Progress's targeted-data method and constrained-shelf qualitative result. Read ReSYNC's skill/concept learning and curriculum assumptions. Update the novelty matrix.
Preregister comparisons
Fix primary methods, budgets, seeds, evaluation layout IDs, success rubric, time caps and stopping rules. Narrow the claim if the pilot shows replanning is sufficient.
Gate 3 and private rehearsal
Create a private 5–10 minute research presentation and a clean pilot demo. Finish the CV/project summary and target-role list; do not send outreach until Week 7.
outputs: Complete adaptation + real-correction loop.
Frozen experiment protocol and literature/novelty matrix.
Private demo and interview presentation ready for the following week.
weeks.gate: Decide the central claim from pilot evidence: faster recovery, better transfer/retention, or better budgeted model correction. If fine-tuning adds no benefit over MPC, report that and pivot to a justified narrower question.
weeks.explain: Why does your method need a few real trials, and which trials should it choose?

weeks.title: Start outreach and run the primary comparison
weeks.aim: Begin researcher conversations after six full weeks while generating the first budget-matched results.
days: Outreach begins
Prepare a concise CV, one-page research summary and preliminary demo. Identify five well-matched teams. Send a small, tailored first batch yourself; track feedback separately from research outcomes.
Lock candidates and budgets
Run active and random selection from the same candidate generator. Verify consistent scoring, legal reset states and real-trial accounting.
Primary methods, seed 1
Evaluate frozen policy, same-model MPC, imagined adaptation and adaptation with random/active correction. Use the prespecified development/evaluation separation.
Primary methods, further seeds
Repeat simulation runs with independent initializations and training seeds. Log compute and adaptation time. Run a limited hardware feasibility block where appropriate.
Coding and research mock
Practice tensor/replay-buffer coding and a 10-minute project explanation. Explain the strongest baseline and what result would invalidate the method.
Weekly evidence review
Generate a preliminary real-success-versus-correction-budget plot with visible uncertainty and sample counts. Tag it preliminary; record all discrepancies and failures.
outputs: First outreach batch after the six-week boundary.
Preliminary budget-matched comparison.
An updated failure taxonomy and experiment ledger.
weeks.gate: The primary comparison is reproducible and fairly budgeted. If selection or labeling is unstable, fix it before collecting more trials.
weeks.explain: How is your experiment different from choosing the best imagined trajectory?

weeks.title: Test generalization and the value of active selection
weeks.aim: Determine whether improvement transfers beyond the correction layouts and whether active selection actually beats random selection.
days: Held-out evaluation
Evaluate the fixed methods on unseen blocker positions and orientations. Keep new geometries as a separately labeled harder split if feasible.
Budget curve
Run nested correction budgets with matched checkpoints. Evaluate at each prespecified point without adding test data to training or choosing trial candidates.
Repeat uncertainty estimates
Collect independent simulation seeds and enough layout diversity to expose variability. Use bootstrap intervals at layout level; report per-layout outcomes.
Hardware block
Run randomized method-order trials with the same reset rubric. Measure operator time, aborted attempts and contact failures; do not infer broad reliability from a small demo.
Interviews and outreach
Follow up on appropriate conversations and practice robotics/RL questions. Use preliminary results without presenting them as accepted publications.
Gate 4 review
Compare active against random, imagined against executed improvement, and adaptation against MPC. Select the smallest set of ablations needed to explain the outcome.
outputs: Held-out generalization results.
Nested correction-budget curve with error bars.
A prioritized ablation list tied to specific hypotheses.
weeks.gate: The core result is stable enough to explain. If active selection is not better, avoid a sample-efficiency claim; investigate calibration, diversity or incorrect candidate scores.
weeks.explain: What exactly is held out, and why does your split test the intended generalization?

weeks.title: Run targeted ablations and interrogate failure
weeks.aim: Understand the mechanism and close the most consequential experimental gaps.
days: Ablation design
Prioritize three ablations: planning versus policy updates; frozen versus corrected world model; active versus random trials. Add one only when it answers a concrete remaining question.
Rollout and model error
Compare short versus longer imagination under the same compute budget. Inspect whether apparent improvement is concentrated where prediction errors are large.
Adaptation and retention
Measure subsequent encounters and nominal-task retention. Test whether learned changes amortize their training time across repeated blockage scenarios.
Failure audit
Review raw trajectories, outcome labels and unsafe/aborted attempts. Check whether the method succeeded by exploiting a reward or evaluation loophole.
Research-system interview
Practice designing the complete deployed loop, including model versioning, timers, reset overhead and rollback. Continue targeted applications and follow-ups.
Gate 5 review
Prepare the figure list and evidence-backed contribution statement. Recheck closely related papers before deciding what is new.
outputs: Three hypothesis-driven ablations.
Retention and amortization measurements.
A draft contribution statement supported by actual evidence.
weeks.gate: Every claimed benefit has a corresponding measurement and baseline. Expand to a second task only if the primary study is complete and repeatable.
weeks.explain: How do you know the improvement came from your correction strategy rather than extra compute or extra data?

weeks.title: Write the story and package a reproducible result
weeks.aim: Turn experiments into a research artifact that can be inspected, rerun and discussed in an interview.
days: Paper skeleton
Draft problem, setting, method and experiments. Lead with the concrete failure and the measured outcome. State observation/model assumptions and the hardware scope.
Results and limitations
Create publication-quality figures from logged results. Write failure cases and negative findings alongside successes. Separate simulated, physical and illustrative figures.
Reproduction recipe
Run the core pipeline from a clean environment. Record exact revisions, dependencies, commands, checkpoint provenance and expected output formats.
Demo production
Record a short synchronized imagination-versus-execution video. Include the blockage, base failure, adaptation time, executed recovery and a representative failure.
Interview rehearsal
Practice the 2-, 10- and 30-minute versions of the project. Solve one ML coding exercise and one robotics system-design question.
External-readiness review
Have the draft checked for unsupported claims, data leakage and missing baselines. Prepare the repository and technical report for release when ready.
outputs: Complete first technical-report/paper draft.
Reproduction README and generated figures.
A short, evidence-labeled demo and interview presentation.
weeks.gate: A reviewer can understand exactly what was learned, what was tested and what remains unproven.
weeks.explain: What is the single strongest result, the strongest alternative explanation, and the biggest limitation?

weeks.title: Close evidence gaps and rehearse deeply
weeks.aim: Finish only experiments needed to substantiate the main claims, while increasing interview intensity.
days: Review-driven fixes
Resolve the most important missing comparison or uncertainty issue. Rerun only affected experiments and keep previous results versioned.
Hardware verification
Repeat critical real trials if necessary. Verify that released videos and figures correspond to documented checkpoints, configurations and data.
Artifact cleanup
Remove credentials and private records, document data/model licenses, and create a small redistributable sample dataset with provenance.
Mock interviews
Run one research deep dive and one coding/system-design mock. Write missed questions into a focused review list.
Role-specific preparation
Adapt the project presentation to robot learning, world models or evaluation roles. Research each team's technical focus before interviews.
Gate 6 review
Confirm the release checklist, paper claims, rerun instructions and known failures. Choose a realistic submission route based on evidence and verified venue dates.
outputs: Reviewed technical report and reproducible result bundle.
Role-specific interview presentations.
A short, prioritized list of remaining limitations and next experiments.
weeks.gate: All mandatory release items are complete or explicitly documented as unavailable. A paper submission is conditional on evidence, not on the calendar alone.
weeks.explain: How would you extend this work in an industry team, and what would you deliberately avoid scaling first?

weeks.title: Release the artifact and complete the interview transition
weeks.aim: Deliver a complete public research artifact and communicate the work with precision.
days: Freeze and archive
Tag a reproducible release, archive evaluation manifests and verify that the repository runs from its documented setup.
Publish the artifact
Release code/configurations, paired examples and a technical report. Publish a preprint only if authorship, evidence and relevant institutional requirements are resolved.
Communicate results
Share the final artifact with relevant existing contacts. Keep the claim proportional to the number of tasks, layouts, seeds and physical trials.
Interview practice
Repeat the weakest coding, RL or robotics topics from mock interviews. Practice concise answers with concrete examples from the project.
Research roadmap
Write a one-page continuation plan covering richer contact, model fidelity, additional embodiments and efficient policy adaptation.
Retrospective
Audit what you can derive, implement, explain and reproduce. Update career materials with completed results rather than planned achievements.
outputs: Versioned public code/configuration release and technical report.
Two-minute demo and 10-minute technical presentation.
Interview-ready knowledge map and evidence-backed project narrative.
weeks.gate: The artifact exists and its claims can be inspected. Use the remaining calendar buffer for integration delays, interviews or a critical rerun—not an unplanned expansion.
weeks.explain: What did you learn that would change how a deployed robot should use its world model?

modules.title: Robotics foundations
modules.question: What connects a policy output to motion of a real end effector?
topics: Reference frames; SE(3), rotation matrices, quaternions, transform composition and camera-to-robot calibration.
Forward and inverse kinematics; Jacobians, singularities, joint limits and task-space versus joint-space commands.
Joint position, velocity and torque control; Cartesian impedance; where a learned policy sits above the controller.
Observations, controller frequency, action duration, latency and synchronization. Review dynamics conceptually rather than spending weeks deriving every manipulator equation.
derive: Compose camera→base and object→camera transforms to obtain an object pose in the robot frame.
Derive the planar two-link Jacobian and a damped least-squares IK update.
Explain why the same Cartesian delta can produce very different joint motion near a singularity.
modules.implement: Write forward kinematics and a Jacobian, verify derivatives numerically, and command an end-effector delta in simulation. Keep units and frame conventions in a single configuration file.
interview: What breaks if an action is interpreted in the wrong frame?
When would you use impedance rather than position control?
How do calibration error and action latency appear in robot-learning data?
modules.gate: Explain the complete observation→policy→controller→robot loop and demonstrate a frame transform with a numerical check.

modules.title: RL essentials and credit assignment
modules.question: What is actually optimized when a robot learns from experience?
topics: MDPs versus POMDPs; return, discount, occupancy and the difference between state and observation.
Bellman expectation and optimality; Monte Carlo versus TD; bootstrapping, bias and variance.
Policy gradients, baselines, advantage estimation and actor–critic methods.
Exploration, replay, reward design, reward hacking, sparse success signals and termination versus time-limit truncation.
derive: Write and solve a small Bellman system; check the Bellman residual.
Derive REINFORCE from the likelihood-ratio identity and show why a state-dependent baseline preserves its expectation.
Calculate GAE by hand on a short trajectory, distinguishing a terminal state from a truncated rollout.
modules.implement: Solve a tiny blocked gridworld exactly, then add a new wall while keeping the goal fixed. Compare evaluating the old policy with replanning the policy. Use the included Bellman example before a neural implementation.
interview: Why can a policy have high training return yet fail under a small obstruction?
What is the bias–variance trade-off in TD learning?
How does partial observability change your agent design?
modules.gate: Derive the Bellman equation and policy gradient unaided; produce a reproducible tabular result.

modules.title: PPO, SAC and stable optimization
modules.question: Which policy update is appropriate for continuous robot actions?
topics: PPO: rollout collection, old log-probabilities, clipped objective, value loss, entropy and advantage normalization.
SAC: twin critics, target networks, replay, entropy temperature and reparameterized tanh-Gaussian actions.
Why clipping is not a hard trust-region guarantee; why off-policy learning is attractive when robot samples are expensive.
Exploding values, observation normalization, reward scale, update-to-data ratio and gradient/debugging diagnostics.
derive: Compute the PPO objective for positive and negative advantages with probability ratios outside the clip interval.
Write the SAC target with entropy correction and explain the minimum of two critics.
Derive the tanh log-density correction and explain why you must not backpropagate through target values.
modules.implement: Implement a small PPO update yourself; use CleanRL to inspect a complete trainer. For SAC, reproduce and modify a maintained implementation rather than rebuilding another full trainer. Compare learning curves and failure modes across seeds.
interview: Why does PPO reuse data only for a limited number of epochs?
Why can an optimistic critic cause failure in imagination?
Which metrics distinguish a broken environment wrapper from a broken learning update?
modules.gate: Explain every tensor in a PPO update and a SAC target, including action and batch dimensions.

modules.title: Imitation, offline RL and robot data
modules.question: How do demonstrations become a robust starting policy?
topics: Behavior cloning; covariate shift; DAgger and corrective demonstrations.
Offline RL, out-of-distribution action values, conservatism, and why arbitrary online updates can destroy a good offline policy.
Episode boundaries, action normalization, camera alignment, observation history and dataset splitting by scene or episode.
Chunked actions, execution horizons, observation horizons and the control trade-off between smoothness and reactivity.
derive: Write BC as maximum likelihood and distinguish single-mode regression from multimodal action distributions.
Explain the source of offline Q-value extrapolation error without memorizing an algorithm name.
Design a split that prevents neighboring video frames leaking between training and evaluation.
modules.implement: Train a BC baseline on unobstructed simulated task demonstrations. Hold out complete layouts and inspect failure videos. Then measure the distribution shift caused by introducing a blocker. Save normalization statistics with the checkpoint.
interview: Why is low validation action error insufficient?
When should you collect corrections instead of adding RL?
How would you audit a robot dataset before training?
modules.gate: A BC checkpoint, a dataset card and an untouched layout-based evaluation split.

modules.title: Generative robot policies and VLAs
modules.question: What do diffusion, flow matching and a VLA change about the action distribution?
topics: Denoising over action chunks; timestep conditioning; noise schedules and iterative action generation.
Conditional flow matching; transport from noise to actions; training objective versus inference ODE steps.
VLA perception-language-action interfaces, proprioception, action representations and embodiment dependence.
Fine-tuning heads/adapters versus the whole model; compute, data and inference-latency constraints.
derive: Explain the conditional diffusion noise-prediction loss and its inputs.
Construct a straight-line conditional flow-matching target between noise and demonstrated actions.
Compare supervised BC updates with RL updates for a generative policy; do not assume PPO log-probabilities are trivial to obtain.
modules.implement: Train a tiny multimodal action denoiser or flow field on synthetic two-route data. Inspect Diffusion Policy's state example and one openpi data adapter. A full VLA fine-tune is a stretch goal after the main research loop works.
interview: Why can averaging two valid robot trajectories create an invalid one?
How do action chunks affect reaction to a new blocker?
Why does adapting a diffusion policy require care with the RL objective?
modules.gate: Explain diffusion policy, flow policy and world-action model without conflating their prediction targets.

modules.title: Learned world models and imagination
modules.question: What must a model predict for imagined training to improve physical behavior?
topics: Action-conditioned transition models; state, image and latent predictions; recurrent belief states under partial observation.
RSSM-style posterior versus prior, reconstruction and predictive losses, reward and continuation heads.
Dreamer-style actor learning in imagined rollouts versus DINO-WM-style planning with learned visual features.
Compounding error, exposure bias, rollout horizon, model exploitation and the difference between a realistic video and useful dynamics.
derive: Write p(z[t+1] | z[t], a[t]) and an observation-conditioned posterior, explaining what is available at deployment.
Explain the components of a latent world-model loss and what each can fail to preserve.
Draw the computational graph for a frozen world model and a trainable actor; specify whether learning uses differentiable rollouts or a synthetic-transition replay buffer.
modules.implement: Fit a small ensemble to blocked and unblocked transitions. Evaluate multi-step errors and success/failure discrimination, not just one-step loss. Add a frozen visual encoder only after the state-based diagnostic is working; make clear which result uses which observations.
interview: Why can a model reconstruct an obstacle yet predict motion through it?
When do you update the model, its current latent state, or the policy?
Why might longer imagination improve reward and worsen physical success?
modules.gate: Replay a matched real/simulator transition and its imagined counterpart; explain a failure at contact or blockage.

modules.title: Planning, control and policy adaptation
modules.question: When is searching for a new action sequence enough, and when is learning worthwhile?
topics: Receding-horizon control; CEM, random shooting and MPPI at a conceptual level.
Configuration-space obstacles, RRT intuition, contact modes, non-prehensile manipulation and geometric feasibility.
Task/skill sequencing versus continuous action optimization; symbolic versus neural world models.
Transient replanning versus persistent policy updates; retention, transfer, compute amortization and total recovery latency.
derive: Write an MPC objective with goal progress, control cost and constraint costs, and identify the horizon and terminal term.
Derive CEM's elite mean/variance update and explain the warm start.
Explain a case in which moving away from the goal is necessary to eventually reach it.
modules.implement: Build CEM-MPC on the same learned dynamics used by the adaptation agent. Keep model calls, horizon, initial observations and wall-clock budget visible. Add an exact-physics oracle only as a diagnostic upper bound.
interview: What would persuade you that policy fine-tuning adds value over replanning?
How do you distinguish a missing skill from a poorly chosen skill sequence?
Why are local trajectory optimizers vulnerable to blocked paths?
modules.gate: A running planner baseline and a fair comparison protocol for training in imagination.

modules.title: Uncertainty, active correction and evaluation
modules.question: Which few physical trials most improve the next recovery?
topics: Epistemic versus aleatoric uncertainty; ensembles; disagreement versus calibrated uncertainty.
Active learning under policy-induced distribution shift; uncertainty sampling versus expected decision improvement.
Model optimism, failure discrimination, Brier score, success reliability and predicted-versus-observed outcomes.
Paired comparisons, bootstrap intervals, layout-level independence, seed variation, cost accounting and negative results.
derive: Define predicted-minus-observed success gap without assuming the cause is intentional self-deception.
Write one simple acquisition score using predicted success and ensemble disagreement; specify candidate-generation and normalization.
Derive a Bernoulli standard error and explain why many trials from one layout are not many independent tasks.
modules.implement: Compare active selection with random selection from the same candidate pool and the same real-trial budget. Fit score weights on development data only. Keep the final evaluation set inaccessible to trial selection and stopping decisions.
interview: Can all ensemble members confidently share the same error?
What does active selection optimize, and what would falsify its benefit?
Why can a lower optimism gap coexist with a worse success rate?
modules.gate: One reproducible budget curve with uncertainty, separate data splits and a complete robot/compute cost ledger.

modules.title: Research engineering and deployment
modules.question: Can someone else rerun, debug and trust your experiment?
topics: PyTorch shapes, autograd boundaries, checkpointing, evaluation mode, vectorized environments and reproducible random generators.
Dataset manifests, immutable split IDs, versioned configs, model hashes and replay-buffer provenance.
Training throughput, GPU memory, inference latency, parallel rollout generation and stale observations.
Robot interfaces, observation/action contracts, episode logging, reset time, command limits and recovery rollback.
derive: Trace batch×time×feature dimensions through model training, imagined rollout and policy execution.
Identify every source of randomness and every timer in one adaptation episode.
Explain how you would diagnose good synthetic returns but poor hardware results.
modules.implement: Use configuration-driven runs, save artifact manifests, and replay an episode with timestamp and action-unit checks. Log every real trial, including aborted trials, calibration and resets. Build a minimal dataset reader before expanding collection.
interview: How do you profile a slow imagination-training loop?
What belongs in a checkpoint besides network weights?
How would you reproduce a failure that only occurs on the physical arm?
modules.gate: A clean-machine setup recipe and an experiment bundle that includes configuration, seeds, code revision and outcome labels.

labs.title: A blocked gridworld and Bellman backups
labs.brief: Make the obstruction precise before adding neural networks. Keep the start and goal fixed; change only a wall or passage.
steps: Implement deterministic transitions and value iteration with an explicit terminal state.
Evaluate the original policy after adding the wall. Then recompute the policy using the updated dynamics.
Plot or print the original path, blocked attempt and revised path; inspect Bellman residuals.
Explain why this experiment demonstrates replanning rather than learning a missing skill.
checks: All transition rows sum to one; the terminal value stays zero.
The added wall invalidates the original route while a longer valid route remains.
Rerunning with the same input produces the same path and values.
labs.output: A tiny reproducible obstruction example and a short explanation of policy evaluation versus policy improvement.
labs.stretch: Replace the detour with a movable blocker and add a push action. Analyze the change in state and action spaces.

labs.title: Frames, kinematics and an IK controller
labs.brief: Build enough geometric intuition to debug a robot policy's actions instead of treating the controller as a black box.
steps: Implement planar two-link forward kinematics and the analytical Jacobian.
Check the Jacobian against finite differences and run damped least-squares IK.
Compose two homogeneous transforms and verify inverse/composition identities.
Repeat the end-effector reaching example in the chosen simulator and document action units and frames.
checks: Jacobian error is below a declared numerical tolerance at nonsingular configurations.
IK converges on reachable targets and reports failure for an unreachable target.
A positive command moves the end effector in the documented frame.
labs.output: A geometry notebook, numerical checks and a diagram of camera, base, tool and object frames.
labs.stretch: Compare joint-space and Cartesian commands near a singularity.

labs.title: Policy gradients, GAE and a PPO update
labs.brief: Own the update equations; reuse the surrounding training infrastructure.
steps: Implement discounted returns and GAE on hand-written trajectories.
Implement clipped policy loss, value loss, entropy and approximate KL with explicit old log-probabilities.
Read CleanRL's PPO file end to end; run one small Gymnasium task and log seeds/configs.
Make one controlled intervention: remove advantage normalization or change the clipping coefficient and explain the effect.
checks: Hand-computed advantages match code, including time-limit bootstrapping.
No gradient reaches the stored old policy log-probabilities or targets.
At least three seeds produce learning curves; a single lucky run is not a claim of convergence.
labs.output: A small original PPO update and an annotated reproducibility report, not a second general-purpose RL library.
labs.stretch: Run continuous-action PPO and inspect action scaling; skip if the week's timebox is exhausted.

labs.title: SAC, replay and continuous actions
labs.brief: Use a reference SAC implementation as the continuous-control workhorse for later residual policy adaptation.
steps: Trace the actor, two critics, target critics, replay sampling and entropy-temperature update.
Run a small continuous-control benchmark using the repository's documented environment.
Inspect the tanh-Gaussian log-probability and action rescaling. Write one numerical comparison.
Save/reload the actor and normalization state and evaluate on fixed initial states.
checks: Target values are detached; replay data and imagined data have explicit provenance.
Train/evaluation action conventions match.
You can explain the minimum-Q target and diagnose value explosion.
labs.output: A pinned configuration and baseline run with an annotated SAC dataflow diagram.
labs.stretch: Test a small residual actor on top of a fixed base controller.

labs.title: Robot interface and episode recorder
labs.brief: Create the shared interface every baseline will use. Finish a simulator episode before extensive collection.
steps: Define observe(), act(), reset() and step() with frame, units, timestamps and frequency documented.
Record observations, executed actions, raw policy outputs, rewards, termination, collision/contact events and scene IDs.
Save an episode manifest including calibration/configuration/checkpoint hashes and source = real, simulator or imagined.
Replay the log offline; identify dropped frames, timestamp inversions and action saturation.
checks: A second reader can load and visualize an episode without launching the robot.
Commanded and executed actions are distinguished.
All aborted attempts remain in the cost ledger; none silently disappear from outcome statistics.
labs.output: One interface, one validated episode schema and an inspection video.
labs.stretch: Export a verified subset to the LeRobot dataset format; do not delay the pilot for format conversion.

labs.title: Behavior cloning and distribution shift
labs.brief: Establish what the policy can already do before you claim it improves in imagination.
steps: Collect or generate 50–100 simple demonstration trajectories in simulation; choose hardware counts only after timing resets.
Train a small MLP BC policy on state observations, or a frozen visual encoder plus policy head.
Split by layout/episode and evaluate closed-loop completion, not frame-level action error alone.
Introduce held-out blocker placements and classify failures into perception, planning, contact/control and missing-skill cases.
checks: No held-out layout is used to choose checkpoints or acquisition weights.
Normalization uses the training split only.
The baseline succeeds on the nominal task often enough to make recovery meaningful.
labs.output: A BC checkpoint, dataset card and nominal-versus-obstructed evaluation grid.
labs.stretch: Add corrective demonstrations and compare them with the same number of ordinary demonstrations.

labs.title: A multimodal action generator
labs.brief: Connect your generative-modeling background to robot action distributions without spending the month training a foundation model.
steps: Create a synthetic dataset with two valid routes around an obstacle.
Train a conditional denoiser or a tiny flow-matching vector field over action chunks.
Compare samples against an MSE regressor whose mean may cross the obstacle.
Inspect one real Diffusion Policy state example and one openpi observation/action adapter.
checks: Plot sampled trajectories and collision rates; visual quality alone is insufficient.
Explain the training objective and sampling loop unaided.
Separate observation horizon, prediction horizon and executed action prefix.
labs.output: A small action-distribution figure and a two-minute explanation suitable for an interview.
labs.stretch: Train the repository's PushT policy only if the research baseline is already running.

labs.title: An action-conditioned dynamics ensemble
labs.brief: Start with a transparent learned dynamics model; expose its failure at the new obstruction.
steps: Fit three small models to delta-state transitions, with bootstrapped episode-level datasets.
Train and evaluate on nominal and blocked transitions; preserve the training/development/test split.
Compare one-step error with 5/10/20-step rollout errors and failure/success discrimination.
Add a frozen visual encoder and latent dynamics if the sensor pathway and compute permit. Record this as a separate observation setting.
checks: An action permutation or zero-action intervention changes predictions appropriately.
The model retains the blocker and distinguishes collisions from progress on development cases.
All ensemble members are independently initialized; disagreement is not claimed to be a calibrated confidence interval.
labs.output: Paired predicted/executed trajectories, multi-step error curves and a documented model limitation.
labs.stretch: Reproduce a small Dreamer/DINO-WM run; full recurrent visual modeling is optional until the core loop works.

labs.title: CEM-MPC as the essential baseline
labs.brief: Test whether the current learned model can solve the obstruction through search before adding policy updates.
steps: Sample bounded action sequences and score them with the learned dynamics and the same task objective used by adaptation.
Refit elite action mean/variance, execute only the first action or chunk, and reobserve.
Warm-start from the remaining previous plan; log model calls and wall-clock latency.
Compare with random shooting and exact-physics planning as a diagnostic. Label the included 2-D point example as a teaching demo, not a robot benchmark.
checks: No future true state leaks into the learned-model planner.
Planner and adaptation agent receive the same current observations and comparable compute budgets.
Costs, horizon and action limits are saved in the run configuration.
labs.output: A planner baseline and a plot of success versus planning compute.
labs.stretch: Add a tree-search baseline only if CEM is demonstrably limited by long-horizon search.

labs.title: Actual policy fine-tuning inside the model
labs.brief: Demonstrate parameter updates that persist after returning to execution; do not relabel action-sequence search as fine-tuning.
steps: Snapshot the base actor and start each adaptation comparison from the same checkpoint.
Infer the current model state from recent observations. Generate short imagined rollouts from real/development anchor states.
Freeze dynamics within an adaptation round. Fine-tune a residual actor using synthetic transitions and a documented SAC-style update; retain a mix of original replay for retention.
Evaluate in the actual simulator or robot, then compare predicted improvement with executed improvement. Enforce an update/time budget and keep rollback available.
checks: Actor weights change; world-model parameters remain fixed within the round.
Real samples, synthetic samples and reused samples have separate counters.
Report recovery on both the current blockage and untouched retention tasks.
labs.output: The first dream→update→execute experiment, including one complete failure analysis.
labs.stretch: Substitute a generative policy adapter only after the compact continuous actor is validated.

labs.title: Choose the next few physical trials
labs.brief: Turn the earlier honesty project into a concrete, budget-matched correction experiment.
steps: Generate a fixed candidate pool from the current policy and legal development layouts.
Define a transparent score: predicted success multiplied by outcome disagreement; use a diversity filter so top selections are not duplicates.
Compare with uniform random selection from the same pool. Count selection compute and aborted real attempts.
Add real transitions, update the world model between rounds, then repeat policy adaptation. Keep score weights fixed before final evaluation.
checks: Selection never reads actual candidate outcomes before choosing.
Active and random conditions start from the same base data and use the same real-trial allowance.
Do not use held-out test layouts to tune the acquisition score or stop training.
labs.output: A candidate-ranking example and a nested correction-budget curve.
labs.stretch: Compare uncertainty-only and policy-rollout refresh after the primary active-versus-random comparison is complete.

labs.title: An honest evaluation report
labs.brief: Produce conclusions that survive a skeptical research interview.
steps: Aggregate by held-out layout and training seed; retain raw outcomes.
Plot real success versus correction trials, recovery latency and total model calls.
Report model optimism, success/failure discrimination and nominal-task retention together.
Use layout-level paired bootstrap intervals for method differences. Declare small hardware evaluations preliminary rather than inferring significance from a few episodes.
checks: All methods use the same success rubric, reset procedure and evaluation layouts.
Hyperparameter tuning and checkpoint selection use development data only.
A clean rerun recreates the figures from logged data; example numbers are never presented as experimental results.
labs.output: A reproducible results bundle with ablations, uncertainty and negative cases.
labs.stretch: Package the paired imagined/real dataset and a model/data card for release.
